svg.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm: Min-Heap Extraction, Edge Relaxation, and Stale Entry Skip
svg.desc: Animated step-by-step trace of Dijkstra's algorithm on a 6-node graph showing min-heap extraction, edge relaxation dist[v] = min(dist[v], dist[u] + w), skipping a stale heap entry (4, B), the settled shortest-path tree, and an A* heuristic extension note.
svg.text: Dijkstra's Algorithm: Min-Heap Extraction, Edge Relaxation & Stale Entry Skip
Greedy Monotonicity Invariant: non-negative weights w(u, v) >= 0 ensure popped vertices never improve later
Weighted Graph G = (V, E) · Source s = A

g.text: STEP 1/6: Pop (0, A) -> settle A; relax A->B (4), A->C (1); push (1,C), (4,B)
STEP 2/6: Pop (1, C) -> relax C->B: 1+2=3 < 4! Push (3, B); (4, B) becomes stale
STEP 3/6: Pop (3, B) -> settle B; relax B->D: 3+2=5; push (5, D)
STEP 4/6: Pop (4, B) -> STALE! B already finalized at dist[B]=3 -> SKIP
STEP 5/6: Pop (5, D) -> settle D; relax D->F: 5+3=8; push (8, F)
STEP 6/6: Pop (6, E), (8, F) -> E->F (6+4=10 > 8, skip); SPT finalized!

svg.text: Lazy Deletion & Why Stale Heap Entries Are Safe to Skip
1. Standard binary heaps push a new pair (3, B) instead of O(log V) decrease-key on (4, B).
2. When stale (4, B) is popped later, popped_d (4) > dist[B] (3) or B is already finalized -> skip in O(1).
Warning: Negative edge w(x,y) < 0 breaks monotonicity, allowing settled nodes to relax again.
* Stale duplicate entry left in heap until popped; discarded by seen/dist check.
Optimal path A -> F: A -> C (1) -> B (3) -> D (5) -> F (8). Total cost = 8.
A* Goal-Directed Extension: f(n) = g(n) + h(n)
• Admissible: h(n) <= d(n, goal) guarantees optimal path on tree search.
• Consistent (Monotonic): h(n) <= c(n, p) + h(p) -> no re-opening closed nodes.
Dijkstra is A* with h(n) = 0 across all vertices.
O((V + E) log V) · O(V + E)
Key Invariant: Each vertex is finalized at most once; each edge relaxes at most once when popped in non-decreasing dist[u] order.
